about.heading: About me
about.html:
I’m a visual artist focused on animation and motion design. I mix new tools with traditional craft to create visuals that feel fresh, distinctive, and built with intention.

Over the years, I’ve worked across music, advertising, and independent projects. I’ve created projection mapped visuals, branded content, and fully animated music videos, often taking things from the first idea all the way to final delivery. I like pushing concepts past the obvious and finding the version that feels bold and clear. Sometimes that means building experimental looks in ComfyUI, sometimes it is character work in Toon Boom, and sometimes it is shaping the final polish in After Effects and DaVinci.

At the core, I care about storytelling and imagination. I love taking a simple concept and turning it into something that feels alive, something that pulls people in and makes them stop for a moment.

I’m always open to new collaborations with brands, agencies, and other creatives. If you have a project you want to bring to life, I’d love to connect.

Read more.

zealot.heading: ZEALOT: my animated short film
zealot.html:
Excited to share ZEALOT, my sci fi revenge story told as an animated music video. This was a full creative odyssey. I directed, wrote, animated, and handled post production myself, blending traditional animation with a hybrid pipeline using Cinema 4D, ComfyUI, Toon Boom, After Effects, and DaVinci.

Big shoutout to Trey Russell for trusting me with his song and giving me the creative freedom to build the story and world. If you are into 90s animation and sci fi world building, I think you will enjoy this one.

about.heading: About
paras: I'm a video editor and motion designer working on performance ads, animation and music videos. I spent the last stretch as the Spanish-line editor at Bublishing, shipping direct-response ads at volume and building the AI footage pipeline the team now runs on. Before that: projection-mapped live visuals, branded content and fully animated music videos, usually from first idea to final delivery.

I mix new tools with traditional craft. Sometimes that means an experimental look built in ComfyUI, sometimes character work in Toon Boom or Cinema 4D, sometimes the final polish in After Effects and DaVinci. What stays constant is storytelling: a simple idea turned into something that makes people stop.
Based in Lima, regularly in Madrid, working remotely with teams in the US and Europe. Open to full-time and contract roles in performance creative, motion and AI video.

casestudy.title: AI footage pipeline for direct-response ads — case study — Diego Salas
casestudy.description: How Diego Salas built a repeatable AI footage pipeline (Higgsfield/Seedance, Google Flow, ComfyUI) for Spanish-language direct-response ads at Bublishing, adopted by the whole editor team.
casestudy.heading: AI footage pipeline for direct-response ads
casestudy.lede: A repeatable way to generate UGC-style and medical-animation footage for Spanish-language ads without the “too AI” look. Built in my first months at Bublishing, documented, and adopted by the whole editor team.

p: Bublishing produced direct-response ads at volume for natural-health offers in English and Spanish. The Spanish line needed presenter footage, product shots and medical animations that didn't exist as stock, fast enough to ship dozens of variations a month.

Early generated footage looked artificial, which hurt ad realism and burned generation credits on takes nobody could use. Spanish prompts drifted into English-market visuals when the starting frames and prompt framing were North American.

ul: A prompt system with two rule sets, UGC (handheld realism, native Spanish speakers, LATAM settings) and medical (clean animation, anatomically plausible, no text artefacts), applied to every shot before generation.

Generation on Higgsfield / Seedance 2.0 at 3:4, 8 s, 720p, with a fallback route when a shot wouldn't resolve; Google Flow for Spanish-language dialogue shots after diagnosing the language-drift problem; ComfyUI on RunPod for experimental looks.

The whole flow driven from Claude: the concept's shot list goes in, cleaned prompts come out, clips are generated, downloaded, audio-stripped and filed into the concept folder, numbered and ready for the edit.
120+ ad variations shipped in three months, 82 of them in one month, on $14k+ of monthly spend.
Documented the full UGC and medical prompt system and shared it in the editor channel; the Spanish team adopted it. Coached a teammate on the workflow and ran QC on her output.
Proposed moving the team's generation plan to annual billing with a capped auto-refill: about $670 a year saved and no more running out of credits mid-session.

p: Higgsfield / Seedance 2.0, Google Flow, ComfyUI + RunPod, Claude, DaVinci Resolve, After Effects.
